items.headline: Palace × Burberry: peak British collab
items.caption: A surprise 10-piece capsule from two UK icons.
body: The skate brand and the heritage house dropped the collab with no warning.
It continues Burberry's comeback by leaning into its Britishness.
How to wear it: a check scarf with a skate hoodie.

items.headline: Red Wing and BEAMS bring back a '90s boot
items.caption: A fan-favourite boot unseen for 30 years, for BEAMS' 50th.
body: BEAMS reinterprets American style through a Japanese lens.
This revival plays straight to long-time fans.
How to wear it: raw denim, cuffed, and a flannel shirt.

items.headline: Comme des Garçons tones down New Balance's wildest shoe
items.caption: The 1890A 'snocassin', half sneaker, half moccasin, now in calm black and white.
body: The 1890A launched this summer in loud snakeskin, cow print and silver mesh.
CDG Homme keeps the odd shape but turns the colour right down, as it has with Nike and Asics.
How to wear it: wide black trousers and a white tee.

items.headline: Lemaire's best product may be its art shows
items.caption: A Surrealist exhibition in its Paris flagship, with a matching capsule.
body: The Paris store shows work by painter Roland Topor.
Lemaire's shops feel like a stylish friend's home.
How to wear it: Lemaire's relaxed tailoring, muted colours, nothing tight.

items.headline: Nike's Air Max Plus 'Glasgow' nods to the traffic cone
items.caption: A city sneaker with in-jokes only Glaswegians will spot.
body: It follows last month's Air Max 95 'Liverpool' made with JD Sports.
It honours the famous cone that sits on the Duke of Wellington statue.
How to wear it: tracksuit, Air Max, and a straight face.

items.headline: Onitsuka Tiger's furry Mexico 66
items.caption: The classic sneaker covered in faux fur, in five colours.
body: The Mexico 66 Paraty comes in shades like 'Cotton Candy', 'Airy Blue' and 'Brown Storm'.
Faux fur runs across the upper and inside the shoe.
How to wear it: brave move; keep the rest of the outfit very plain.

items.headline: Nike's Moon Shoe goes balletcore
items.caption: Pink satin uppers and frilly laces on Nike's oldest sneaker.
body: The 'Light Carnation' Moon Shoe keeps its slim Waffle sole.
Satin replaces the usual nylon.
How to wear it: if you dare, with black trousers to let it shine.

items.headline: GQ's four big new watches this month
items.caption: Moser goes retrograde, Lange brings back a bracelet, Biver goes hand-wound, Breitling goes vintage.
body: H. Moser & Cie adds three models with retrograde seconds to its Streamliner line.
A. Lange & Söhne revives a much-loved bracelet; Biver drops its first hand-wound three-hand watch.
How to wear it: one serious watch, simple clothes, no other wrist clutter.

items.headline: Ballon d'Or trophies arrive in Louis Vuitton trunks
items.caption: Harry Kane and Alexia Putellas's trophies came in bespoke LV cases.
body: The custom trunks are now a Ballon d'Or tradition.
This year's ceremony was in London.
Style lesson: good luggage is a statement.

items.headline: Michael Carrick's touchline style
items.caption: Man United are struggling, but their manager's wardrobe isn't.
body: United sit 16th after a 3–0 home loss to Bournemouth.
Carrick's sideline outfits are still sharp.
How to wear it: a dark overcoat over a fine knit.

items.headline: Tom Hardy's 'MobLand' jackets
items.caption: From field jackets to leather, how to dress like the show's fixer.
body: Hardy plays Harry Da Souza in Guy Ritchie's mob drama, now in season two.
His outerwear does a lot of the talking.
How to wear it: a worn-in leather jacket over a plain tee.

items.headline: Church's turns a Marylebone pub into a shoe club
items.caption: British shoemaker Church's hosted a gin-and-leather evening at The Hart in London.
body: Church's Club brought its traditional style to a cosy pub lock-in in Marylebone.
The night mixed British heritage, gin tasting and very good footwear.
How to wear it: polished brogues, grey flannel trousers and a navy knit.

items.headline: Japan's best potato harvest in a decade
items.caption: Hokkaido bucked a summer of crop failures.
body: Ideal heat and rain made Hokkaido almost the only Northern Hemisphere region to grow more potatoes.
Snack maker Calbee expects to hit its usual 250,000 tons.
Good news for crisps everywhere.

items.headline: A Texas school is named after its janitor
items.caption: 'Miss Marilyn' Hampton worked 39 years at Aubrey schools.
body: She was the first of seven siblings to graduate high school, but often felt like a failure for not going to college.
The district honoured her by naming a new school after her.
Her superintendent says she 'is truly Aubrey ISD'.

items.headline: An exam question led a student to a mentor
items.caption: A strawberry farmer's number in an English test inspired a future AI student.
body: He Ziqi called the Beijing farmer's number from a reading passage, just to check it.
The farmer turned the calls into chances to inspire students.
He is now a postgraduate student in AI.
